paper.title: As We May Think
paper.author: Vannevar Bush
paper.description: 在个人电脑出现之前，设想一张可以储存资料、批注并连接阅读线索的书桌。

glossary.memex: Memex（设想中的个人知识工具）

blocks.en: As Director of the Office of Scientific Research and Development, Dr. Vannevar Bush has coordinated the activities of some six thousand leading American scientists in the application of science to warfare. In this significant article he holds up an incentive for scientists when the fighting has ceased. He urges that men of science should then turn to the massive task of making more accessible our bewildering store of knowledge.
blocks.zh: 作为科学研究与发展办公室主任，万尼瓦尔·布什博士协调了约六千名美国杰出科学家，将科学应用于战争。在这篇重要文章中，他为战斗结束后的科学家提出了一个努力目标。他敦促科学工作者转而承担一项艰巨任务：使我们数量庞大、令人困惑的知识储备更容易利用。

blocks.en: For years inventions have extended man's physical powers rather than the powers of his mind. Trip hammers that multiply the fists, microscopes that sharpen the eye, and engines of destruction and detection are new results, but not the end results, of modern science. Now, says Dr. Bush, instruments are at hand which, if properly developed, will give man access to and command over the inherited knowledge of the ages. The perfection of these pacific instruments should be the first objective of our scientists as they emerge from their war work. Like Emerson's famous address of 1837 on "The American Scholar," this paper by Dr. Bush calls for a new relationship between thinking man and the sum of our knowledge. —THE EDITOR
blocks.zh: 多年来，发明扩展的主要是人的体力，而非心智。成倍增强拳力的机械锤、让眼睛看得更清楚的显微镜，以及用于摧毁和探测的装置，都是现代科学的新成果，却不是其最终成果。布什博士说，如今已有一些工具，只要得到适当发展，就能使人们获取并掌握历代传承的知识。科学家走出战争工作时，完善这些和平用途的工具，应成为首要目标。正如爱默生1837年那篇著名的《美国学者》演讲，布什的文章呼吁在思考的人与我们全部知识之间，建立一种新的关系。——编者

blocks.en: This has not been a scientist's war; it has been a war in which all have had a part. The scientists, burying their old professional competition in the demand of a common cause, have shared greatly and learned much. It has been exhilarating to work in effective partnership. Now, for many, this appears to be approaching an end. What are the scientists to do next?
blocks.zh: 这不是只属于科学家的战争，而是一场人人都有参与的战争。科学家为了共同事业，搁置了过去的专业竞争，广泛分享，也学到了很多。有效合作令人振奋。如今，对许多人来说，这一切似乎即将结束。科学家接下来该做些什么？

blocks.en: For the biologists, and particularly for the medical scientists, there can be little indecision, for their war has hardly required them to leave the old paths. Many indeed have been able to carry on their war research in their familiar peacetime laboratories. Their objectives remain much the same.
blocks.zh: 生物学家，尤其医学科学家，大概没有多少犹豫，因为战争几乎没有迫使他们离开原有的道路。许多人甚至能在熟悉的和平时期实验室里继续战争研究。他们的目标大致没有改变。

blocks.en: It is the physicists who have been thrown most violently off stride, who have left academic pursuits for the making of strange destructive gadgets, who have had to devise new methods for their unanticipated assignments. They have done their part on the devices that made it possible to turn back the enemy, have worked in combined effort with the physicists of our allies. They have felt within themselves the stir of achievement. They have been part of a great team. Now, as peace approaches, one asks where they will find objectives worthy of their best.
blocks.zh: 被最猛烈地打乱步调的是物理学家。他们离开学术研究，制造奇异的破坏性装置，必须为出乎意料的任务发明新方法。他们为使我们得以击退敌人的装备尽了自己的力量，并与盟国物理学家合作。他们在内心感受到成就的激动，成为一支伟大团队的一部分。如今和平将至，人们要问：他们将在哪里找到值得全力以赴的目标？
一

blocks.en: Of what lasting benefit has been man's use of science and of the new instruments which his research brought into existence? First, they have increased his control of his material environment. They have improved his food, his clothing, his shelter; they have increased his security and released him partly from the bondage of bare existence. They have given him increased knowledge of his own biological processes so that he has had a progressive freedom from disease and an increased span of life. They are illuminating the interactions of his physiological and psychological functions, giving the promise of an improved mental health.
blocks.zh: 人类运用科学，以及研究产生的新工具，获得了哪些持久的益处？首先，它们增强了人对物质环境的控制。它们改善了食物、衣着和住所，提高了安全性，使人部分摆脱仅仅维持生存的束缚。它们加深了人对自身生物过程的认识，使人逐渐免于疾病，寿命不断延长。它们正在阐明生理与心理功能的相互作用，带来改善心理健康的希望。

blocks.en: Science has provided the swiftest communication between individuals; it has provided a record of ideas and has enabled man to manipulate and to make extracts from that record so that knowledge evolves and endures throughout the life of a race rather than that of an individual.
blocks.zh: 科学提供了人与人之间最快捷的通信方式；它保存思想的记录，使人能够处理这些记录并从中摘取内容，从而让知识在人类这一种族的一生中发展、延续，而非仅存在于某个个体的一生。

blocks.en: There is a growing mountain of research. But there is increased evidence that we are being bogged down today as specialization extends. The investigator is staggered by the findings and conclusions of thousands of other workers—conclusions which he cannot find time to grasp, much less to remember, as they appear. Yet specialization becomes increasingly necessary for progress, and the effort to bridge between disciplines is correspondingly superficial.
blocks.zh: 研究正在堆积成越来越高的山。然而，越来越多的证据表明，随着专业化扩展，我们正陷入泥潭。研究者被成千上万其他工作者的发现与结论震撼；这些结论不断出现，他连理解都没有时间，更不用说记住。然而，专业化对进步日益必要，而跨学科沟通的努力也相应变得肤浅。

blocks.en: Professionally our methods of transmitting and reviewing the results of research are generations old and by now are totally inadequate for their purpose. If the aggregate time spent in writing scholarly works and in reading them could be evaluated, the ratio between these amounts of time might well be startling. Those who conscientiously attempt to keep abreast of current thought, even in restricted fields, by close and continuous reading might well shy away from an examination calculated to show how much of the previous month's efforts could be produced on call. Mendel's concept of the laws of genetics was lost to the world for a generation because his publication did not reach the few who were capable of grasping and extending it; and this sort of catastrophe is undoubtedly being repeated all about us, as truly significant attainments become lost in the mass of the inconsequential.
blocks.zh: 我们在专业上用来传播和评述研究结果的方法，已经沿用几代人，如今完全不足以实现目的。如果能够估算撰写学术著作与阅读它们所花的总时间，两者的比值很可能令人吃惊。那些通过细致、持续阅读，认真试图跟上当代思想的人，即便领域很窄，也可能不愿接受一种检验：看看上个月付出的努力，有多少能够随时复述出来。孟德尔的遗传规律思想曾被世界遗忘一代人，因为他的出版物没有到达少数能够理解并发展它的人手中；这种灾难无疑正在我们周围反复发生，真正重要的成就淹没在大量无足轻重的内容里。

blocks.en: The difficulty seems to be, not so much that we publish unduly in view of the extent and variety of present day interests, but rather that publication has been extended far beyond our present ability to make real use of the record. The summation of human experience is being expanded at a prodigious rate, and the means we use for threading through the consequent maze to the momentarily important item is the same as was used in the days of square-rigged ships.
blocks.zh: 困难似乎并不主要在于，相对于当代兴趣的广度和多样性，我们出版得过多，而在于出版规模远远超过了目前实际利用记录的能力。人类经验的总量以惊人的速度增长，而我们从由此产生的迷宫中找到眼下重要条目所用的方法，仍与横帆船时代相同。

blocks.en: But there are signs of a change as new and powerful instrumentalities come into use. Photocells capable of seeing things in a physical sense, advanced photography which can record what is seen or even what is not, thermionic tubes capable of controlling potent forces under the guidance of less power than a mosquito uses to vibrate his wings, cathode ray tubes rendering visible an occurrence so brief that by comparison a microsecond is a long time, relay combinations which will carry out involved sequences of movements more reliably than any human operator and thousands of times as fast—there are plenty of mechanical aids with which to effect a transformation in scientific records.
blocks.zh: 不过，新的强大工具开始投入使用，已经显示出变化的迹象。能够在物理意义上“看见”事物的光电池；能够记录可见、甚至不可见事物的先进摄影技术；只需比蚊子振翅还小的功率，就能控制强大力量的热电子管；把极其短暂的事件显示出来、短暂到相比之下微秒都显得漫长的阴极射线管；比任何操作者都可靠、速度快上数千倍、可以完成复杂动作序列的继电器组合——有许多机械辅助工具，可以推动科学记录的变革。

blocks.en: Two centuries ago Leibnitz invented a calculating machine which embodied most of the essential features of recent keyboard devices, but it could not then come into use. The economics of the situation were against it: the labor involved in constructing it, before the days of mass production, exceeded the labor to be saved by its use, since all it could accomplish could be duplicated by sufficient use of pencil and paper. Moreover, it would have been subject to frequent breakdown, so that it could not have been depended upon; for at that time and long after, complexity and unreliability were synonymous.
blocks.zh: 两百年前，莱布尼茨发明了一台计算机，具备近代键盘装置的大多数基本特征，但当时无法投入使用。经济条件对它不利：在大规模生产出现之前，制造它所需的劳动，超过了使用它能够节省的劳动，因为只要足够使用纸笔，就能重复它所完成的一切。此外，它会频繁故障，无法信赖；在当时以及此后很长时期，复杂性与不可靠几乎是同义词。

blocks.en: Babbage, even with remarkably generous support for his time, could not produce his great arithmetical machine. His idea was sound enough, but construction and maintenance costs were then too heavy. Had a Pharaoh been given detailed and explicit designs of an automobile, and had he understood them completely, it would have taxed the resources of his kingdom to have fashioned the thousands of parts for a single car, and that car would have broken down on the first trip to Giza.
blocks.zh: 巴贝奇即便获得了在当时十分慷慨的资助，也未能造出他那台宏大的算术机器。他的构想足够合理，但制造与维护成本过高。假如有人给一位法老一份详细、明确的汽车设计，而他也完全理解，那么仅为一辆汽车制造数千个部件，就足以耗尽王国的资源，而那辆汽车第一次开往吉萨时就会抛锚。

blocks.en: Machines with interchangeable parts can now be constructed with great economy of effort. In spite of much complexity, they perform reliably. Witness the humble typewriter, or the movie camera, or the automobile. Electrical contacts have ceased to stick when thoroughly understood. Note the automatic telephone exchange, which has hundreds of thousands of such contacts, and yet is reliable. A spider web of metal, sealed in a thin glass container, a wire heated to brilliant glow, in short, the thermionic tube of radio sets, is made by the hundred million, tossed about in packages, plugged into sockets—and it works! Its gossamer parts, the precise location and alignment involved in its construction, would have occupied a master craftsman of the guild for months; now it is built for thirty cents. The world has arrived at an age of cheap complex devices of great reliability; and something is bound to come of it.
blocks.zh: 如今，具有可互换零件的机器，能够以很少的劳动制造出来。尽管十分复杂，它们仍能可靠运行。看看普通的打字机、电影摄影机或汽车吧。对电触点充分理解之后，它们便不再粘连。自动电话交换机拥有数十万个这样的触点，却依然可靠。把金属蛛网封进薄薄的玻璃容器，里面一根导线加热得明亮发光——也就是收音机里的热电子管——这种东西以亿计生产，在包装中被抛来抛去，插进插座，然后就能工作！那些纤细的部件，以及制造所要求的精确定位与对准，过去会让一位行会大师忙上几个月；如今制造只需三十美分。世界已经进入一个廉价、复杂而极为可靠的装置的时代，某些新事物必定由此产生。
二

blocks.en: A record if it is to be useful to science, must be continuously extended, it must be stored, and above all it must be consulted. Today we make the record conventionally by writing and photography, followed by printing; but we also record on film, on wax disks, and on magnetic wires. Even if utterly new recording procedures do not appear, these present ones are certainly in the process of modification and extension.
blocks.zh: 记录若要对科学有用，就必须不断扩充、加以保存，尤其必须被查阅。今天，我们通常通过写作与摄影来制作记录，然后印刷；也在胶片、蜡盘和磁性金属丝上记录。即使不出现全新的记录方式，现有方式也肯定正在改变和扩展。

blocks.en: Certainly progress in photography is not going to stop. Faster material and lenses, more automatic cameras, finer-grained sensitive compounds to allow an extension of the minicamera idea, are all imminent. Let us project this trend ahead to a logical, if not inevitable, outcome. The camera hound of the future wears on his forehead a lump a little larger than a walnut. It takes pictures 3 millimeters square, later to be projected or enlarged, which after all involves only a factor of 10 beyond present practice. The lens is of universal focus, down to any distance accommodated by the unaided eye, simply because it is of short focal length. There is a built-in photocell on the walnut such as we now have on at least one camera, which automatically adjusts exposure for a wide range of illumination. There is film in the walnut for a hundred exposures, and the spring for operating its shutter and shifting its film is wound once for all when the film clip is inserted. It produces its result in full color. It may well be stereoscopic, and record with two spaced glass eyes, for striking improvements in stereoscopic technique are just around the corner.
blocks.zh: 摄影的进步当然不会停止。更快的感光材料与镜头、更自动化的相机，以及能够发展微型相机思想的更细颗粒感光化合物，都即将出现。让我们把这一趋势推向一个合理、虽未必不可避免的结果。未来的摄影爱好者额头上戴着一个比核桃稍大的东西，拍摄边长三毫米的照片，之后再投影或放大；这不过是比现行做法再缩小十倍。由于焦距很短，镜头在肉眼能适应的任何距离上都无需调焦。“核桃”内有一个光电池，如同如今至少有一种相机已经具备的那样，能够在广泛照度范围内自动调整曝光。里面的胶片可拍一百张；插入胶片匣时，就一次性上紧驱动快门与走片的发条。照片是全彩色的，也很可能具有立体效果，通过两个相隔的玻璃眼睛记录，因为立体摄影技术即将取得显著改进。

blocks.en: The cord which trips its shutter may reach down a man's sleeve within easy reach of his fingers. A quick squeeze, and the picture is taken. On a pair of ordinary glasses is a square of fine lines near the top of one lens, where it is out of the way of ordinary vision. When an object appears in that square, it is lined up for its picture. As the scientist of the future moves about the laboratory or the field, every time he looks at something worthy of the record, he trips the shutter and in it goes, without even an audible click. Is this all fantastic? The only fantastic thing about it is the idea of making as many pictures as would result from its use.
blocks.zh: 触发快门的绳索可以沿着衣袖垂下，方便手指触及。轻轻一捏，照片就拍好了。普通眼镜的一个镜片上方，有细线构成的方框，不妨碍正常视野。物体出现在方框中，就已对准拍摄位置。未来的科学家在实验室或野外走动时，每看到值得记录的事物，就触发快门，把它收入记录，甚至没有可听见的咔嗒声。这全是幻想吗？唯一显得夸张的，是使用它将拍下那么多照片的想法。

blocks.en: Will there be dry photography? It is already here in two forms. When Brady made his Civil War pictures, the plate had to be wet at the time of exposure. Now it has to be wet during development instead. In the future perhaps it need not be wetted at all. There have long been films impregnated with diazo dyes which form a picture without development, so that it is already there as soon as the camera has been operated. An exposure to ammonia gas destroys the unexposed dye, and the picture can then be taken out into the light and examined. The process is now slow, but someone may speed it up, and it has no grain difficulties such as now keep photographic researchers busy. Often it would be advantageous to be able to snap the camera and to look at the picture immediately.
blocks.zh: 会有干式摄影吗？它已经以两种形式存在。布雷迪拍摄美国内战照片时，底片在曝光时必须保持湿润。如今，改为显影时需要湿润。未来也许完全不必润湿。早已有浸渍重氮染料的胶片，无须显影就能成像，因此相机一操作，图像就在那里了。暴露于氨气，会破坏未曝光的染料，然后就可以把照片拿到光线下查看。目前这个过程很慢，但也许有人能加快它，而且它没有让摄影研究者忙碌的颗粒问题。能够按下相机后立即查看照片，常常很有好处。

blocks.en: Another process now in use is also slow, and more or less clumsy. For fifty years impregnated papers have been used which turn dark at every point where an electrical contact touches them, by reason of the chemical change thus produced in an iodine compound included in the paper. They have been used to make records, for a pointer moving across them can leave a trail behind. If the electrical potential on the pointer is varied as it moves, the line becomes light or dark in accordance with the potential.
blocks.zh: 另一种已经使用的过程，也很缓慢，且多少有些笨拙。五十年来，人们一直使用一种浸渍处理的纸，电触点碰到哪里，哪里就变黑，这是纸中含有的碘化合物发生化学变化的结果。它们被用来制作记录，因为在纸上移动的触针可以留下轨迹。如果触针移动时电势发生变化，画出的线就随电势而明暗变化。

blocks.en: This scheme is now used in facsimile transmission. The pointer draws a set of closely spaced lines across the paper one after another. As it moves, its potential is varied in accordance with a varying current received over wires from a distant station, where these variations are produced by a photocell which is similarly scanning a picture. At every instant the darkness of the line being drawn is made equal to the darkness of the point on the picture being observed by the photocell. Thus, when the whole picture has been covered, a replica appears at the receiving end.
blocks.zh: 这种方案如今用于传真。触针依次在纸上画出一系列密集的线。它移动时，其电势随远处站点通过导线传来的变化电流而变化；这些电流变化由同样扫描照片的光电池产生。每一时刻，所画线条的暗度都等于光电池正在观察的照片位置的暗度。这样，扫描完整张照片后，接收端就出现了副本。

blocks.en: A scene itself can be just as well looked over line by line by the photocell in this way as can a photograph of the scene. This whole apparatus constitutes a camera, with the added feature, which can be dispensed with if desired, of making its picture at a distance. It is slow, and the picture is poor in detail. Still, it does give another process of dry photography, in which the picture is finished as soon as it is taken.
blocks.zh: 光电池也能用这种方式，逐行扫描景物本身，而不只是景物的照片。整套设备就构成了一台相机，额外具有在远处制作图像的功能；如果不需要，可以省去这一功能。它速度慢，细节也不佳。不过，它确实提供了另一种干式摄影过程，照片拍下时也就制作完成了。

blocks.en: It would be a brave man who would predict that such a process will always remain clumsy, slow, and faulty in detail. Television equipment today transmits sixteen reasonably good pictures a second, and it involves only two essential differences from the process described above. For one, the record is made by a moving beam of electrons rather than a moving pointer, for the reason that an electron beam can sweep across the picture very rapidly indeed. The other difference involves merely the use of a screen which glows momentarily when the electrons hit, rather than a chemically treated paper or film which is permanently altered. This speed is necessary in television, for motion pictures rather than stills are the object.
blocks.zh: 若有人预言这一过程永远会笨拙、缓慢、细节失真，那可真够大胆。今天的电视设备每秒传送十六幅相当不错的图像，与上述过程只有两个基本区别。其一，用移动的电子束，而非移动的触针制作记录，因为电子束确实能非常迅速地扫过图像。另一项区别，仅在于采用电子撞击时短暂发光的屏幕，而非发生永久变化的化学处理纸或胶片。电视需要这种速度，因为目标是活动画面，而非静止照片。

blocks.en: Use chemically treated film in place of the glowing screen, allow the apparatus to transmit one picture only rather than a succession, and a rapid camera for dry photography results. The treated film needs to be far faster in action than present examples, but it probably could be. More serious is the objection that this scheme would involve putting the film inside a vacuum chamber, for electron beams behave normally only in such a rarefied environment. This difficulty could be avoided by allowing the electron beam to play on one side of a partition, and by pressing the film against the other side, if this partition were such as to allow the electrons to go through perpendicular to its surface, and to prevent them from spreading out sideways. Such partitions, in crude form, could certainly be constructed, and they will hardly hold up the general development.
blocks.zh: 用经过化学处理的胶片替代发光屏幕，让装置只传送一幅图像而非连续图像，就得到了一台快速的干式摄影相机。处理过的胶片反应速度必须比现有材料快得多，但很可能能够做到。更严重的问题是，这种方案需要把胶片放进真空室，因为电子束只有在这种稀薄环境中才正常运行。如果隔板能允许电子垂直穿过其表面，又阻止它们横向散开，那么让电子束打在隔板一侧，把胶片压在另一侧，就可以避开这个困难。这种隔板当然能以粗糙的形式制造出来，想必不会阻碍总体发展。

blocks.en: Like dry photography, microphotography still has a long way to go. The basic scheme of reducing the size of the record, and examining it by projection rather than directly, has possibilities too great to be ignored. The combination of optical projection and photographic reduction is already producing some results in microfilm for scholarly purposes, and the potentialities are highly suggestive. Today, with microfilm, reductions by a linear factor of 20 can be employed and still produce full clarity when the material is re-enlarged for examination. The limits are set by the graininess of the film, the excellence of the optical system, and the efficiency of the light sources employed. All of these are rapidly improving.
blocks.zh: 与干式摄影一样，显微摄影还有很长的路要走。缩小记录尺寸、通过投影而非直接查看，这个基本方案具有太大的潜力，不容忽视。光学投影与摄影缩小的结合，已经在学术用途的缩微胶片方面取得一些成果，其潜力很有启发性。如今，缩微胶片可以在线性尺寸上缩小二十倍，重新放大查阅时，仍能保持完全清晰。限制来自胶片的颗粒度、光学系统的质量和所用光源的效率，而这些都在迅速改善。

blocks.en: Assume a linear ratio of 100 for future use. Consider film of the same thickness as paper, although thinner film will certainly be usable. Even under these conditions there would be a total factor of 10,000 between the bulk of the ordinary record on books, and its microfilm replica. The Encyclopoedia Britannica could be reduced to the volume of a matchbox. A library of a million volumes could be compressed into one end of a desk. If the human race has produced since the invention of movable type a total record, in the form of magazines, newspapers, books, tracts, advertising blurbs, correspondence, having a volume corresponding to a billion books, the whole affair, assembled and compressed, could be lugged off in a moving van. Mere compression, of course, is not enough; one needs not only to make and store a record but also be able to consult it, and this aspect of the matter comes later. Even the modern great library is not generally consulted; it is nibbled at by a few.
blocks.zh: 假设未来线性缩小比例为一百。再假设胶片与纸一样厚，尽管肯定可以使用更薄的胶片。即便如此，普通书籍记录与其缩微胶片副本的体积，也会相差一万倍。《大英百科全书》可以缩小到火柴盒大小。拥有百万册书的图书馆，可以压缩进书桌的一端。如果自活字印刷发明以来，人类以杂志、报纸、书籍、小册子、广告宣传和通信等形式产生的全部记录，总体积相当于十亿本书，那么把它们汇集、压缩后，就可以用一辆搬家货车拉走。当然，仅仅压缩还不够；不仅要制作和储存记录，还必须能够查阅，这一点后面再谈。即便现代的大型图书馆，也通常没有得到普遍查阅，只是被少数人一点点啃食。

blocks.en: Compression is important, however, when it comes to costs. The material for the microfilm Britannica would cost a nickel, and it could be mailed anywhere for a cent. What would it cost to print a million copies? To print a sheet of newspaper, in a large edition, costs a small fraction of a cent. The entire material of the Britannica in reduced microfilm form would go on a sheet eight and one-half by eleven inches. Once it is available, with the photographic reproduction methods of the future, duplicates in large quantities could probably be turned out for a cent apiece beyond the cost of materials. The preparation of the original copy? That introduces the next aspect of the subject.
blocks.zh: 不过，涉及成本时，压缩就很重要。缩微胶片版《大英百科全书》的材料只需五美分，花一美分就能寄到任何地方。印制一百万份需要多少成本？大批量印刷一张报纸，成本只是不到一美分的一小部分。整部《大英百科全书》缩微之后，可以放在一张八英寸半乘十一英寸的胶片上。一旦原版具备，利用未来的摄影复制方法，大量复制的成本，在材料费之外，可能每份只要一美分。那么，原版如何制作？这就引出了这个主题的下一个方面。
三

blocks.en: To make the record, we now push a pencil or tap a typewriter. Then comes the process of digestion and correction, followed by an intricate process of typesetting, printing, and distribution. To consider the first stage of the procedure, will the author of the future cease writing by hand or typewriter and talk directly to the record? He does so indirectly, by talking to a stenographer or a wax cylinder; but the elements are all present if he wishes to have his talk directly produce a typed record. All he needs to do is to take advantage of existing mechanisms and to alter his language.
blocks.zh: 现在制作记录，我们拿铅笔写，或敲打字机。接着是消化、修改，再经过复杂的排字、印刷和发行。先考虑程序的第一步：未来的作者是否会停止手写或打字，直接对着记录说话？他通过向速记员或蜡筒说话，已经间接这样做了；而如果希望讲话直接产生打字记录，所需的各种要素也都具备了。他只需利用现有机制，并调整自己的语言。

blocks.en: At a recent World Fair a machine called a Voder was shown. A girl stroked its keys and it emitted recognizable speech. No human vocal chords entered into the procedure at any point; the keys simply combined some electrically produced vibrations and passed these on to a loud-speaker. In the Bell Laboratories there is the converse of this machine, called a Vocoder. The loudspeaker is replaced by a microphone, which picks up sound. Speak to it, and the corresponding keys move. This may be one element of the postulated system.
blocks.zh: 最近的一次世界博览会上，展示了一台称为Voder的机器。一位姑娘按动按键，机器就发出可辨认的语音。整个过程任何环节都没有人的声带参与；按键只是把电产生的某些振动组合起来，传给扬声器。贝尔实验室有一台与它相反的机器，称为Vocoder：扬声器被拾取声音的麦克风替代。对它说话，相应的按键就会动作。这可以成为所设想系统的一个组成部分。

blocks.en: The other element is found in the stenotype, that somewhat disconcerting device encountered usually at public meetings. A girl strokes its keys languidly and looks about the room and sometimes at the speaker with a disquieting gaze. From it emerges a typed strip which records in a phonetically simplified language a record of what the speaker is supposed to have said. Later this strip is retyped into ordinary language, for in its nascent form it is intelligible only to the initiated. Combine these two elements, let the Vocoder run the stenotype, and the result is a machine which types when talked to.
blocks.zh: 另一个组成部分存在于速记机中，这种略让人不安的装置通常在公众会议上见到。一位姑娘懒洋洋地按着键，环顾房间，有时又用令人不安的目光看着演讲者。机器吐出一条打字纸带，以简化的语音语言记录演讲者应该说过的话。之后，这条纸带重新打成普通语言，因为原始形式只有受过训练的人才能看懂。把这两个组成部分结合起来，让Vocoder驱动速记机，就得到一台对它说话便会打字的机器。

blocks.en: Our present languages are not especially adapted to this sort of mechanization, it is true. It is strange that the inventors of universal languages have not seized upon the idea of producing one which better fitted the technique for transmitting and recording speech. Mechanization may yet force the issue, especially in the scientific field; whereupon scientific jargon would become still less intelligible to the layman.
blocks.zh: 的确，我们现有的语言并不特别适合这种机械化。奇怪的是，发明通用语言的人没有抓住这个想法，创造一种更适于语音传输和记录技术的语言。机械化也许最终会迫使人们处理这一问题，尤其在科学领域；到那时，科学术语对外行将变得更加难懂。

blocks.en: One can now picture a future investigator in his laboratory. His hands are free, and he is not anchored. As he moves about and observes, he photographs and comments. Time is automatically recorded to tie the two records together. If he goes into the field, he may be connected by radio to his recorder. As he ponders over his notes in the evening, he again talks his comments into the record. His typed record, as well as his photographs, may both be in miniature, so that he projects them for examination.
blocks.zh: 现在可以想象，未来的研究者在实验室里，双手自由，也不必固定在一个地方。他一边走动观察，一边拍照并作口述评论。时间会自动记录，以把这两种记录联系起来。如果到野外，他可以通过无线电与记录装置连接。晚上思考笔记时，他再把评论说进记录中。打字记录和照片都可以采用微缩形式，因此他通过投影来查看。

blocks.en: Much needs to occur, however, between the collection of data and observations, the extraction of parallel material from the existing record, and the final insertion of new material into the general body of the common record. For mature thought there is no mechanical substitute. But creative thought and essentially repetitive thought are very different things. For the latter there are, and may be, powerful mechanical aids.
blocks.zh: 不过，在收集数据与观察、从既有记录中抽取相关材料，以及最终把新材料加入公共记录整体之间，还有许多事情需要完成。成熟的思考没有机械替代品。但创造性思考与本质上重复性的思考，是很不一样的事情。对于后者，已有、也可能出现强大的机械辅助工具。

blocks.en: Adding a column of figures is a repetitive thought process, and it was long ago properly relegated to the machine. True, the machine is sometimes controlled by a keyboard, and thought of a sort enters in reading the figures and poking the corresponding keys, but even this is avoidable. Machines have been made which will read typed figures by photocells and then depress the corresponding keys; these are combinations of photocells for scanning the type, electric circuits for sorting the consequent variations, and relay circuits for interpreting the result into the action of solenoids to pull the keys down.
blocks.zh: 把一列数字相加，是一种重复性思维过程，早就理所当然地交给了机器。诚然，机器有时由键盘控制，阅读数字、按相应按键时仍需要某种思考，但连这一点也可以避免。已经有机器能用光电池读取打出的数字，再按下相应按键；它们结合了扫描字形的光电池、分辨所产生变化的电路，以及把结果解释为电磁铁拉下按键动作的继电器电路。

blocks.en: All this complication is needed because of the clumsy way in which we have learned to write figures. If we recorded them positionally, simply by the configuration of a set of dots on a card, the automatic reading mechanism would become comparatively simple. In fact if the dots are holes, we have the punched-card machine long ago produced by Hollorith for the purposes of the census, and now used throughout business. Some types of complex businesses could hardly operate without these machines.
blocks.zh: 之所以需要这么复杂，是因为我们学会的数字书写方式很笨拙。如果按位置记录数字，仅用卡片上一组点的排列来表示，自动读取机制就会简单得多。事实上，如果把点变成孔，就得到霍勒里斯很早为人口普查制造、如今广泛用于商业的穿孔卡片机器。某些复杂行业，几乎离开这些机器就无法运行。

blocks.en: Adding is only one operation. To perform arithmetical computation involves also subtraction, multiplication, and division, and in addition some method for temporary storage of results, removal from storage for further manipulation, and recording of final results by printing. Machines for these purposes are now of two types: keyboard machines for accounting and the like, manually controlled for the insertion of data, and usually automatically controlled as far as the sequence of operations is concerned; and punched-card machines in which separate operations are usually delegated to a series of machines, and the cards then transferred bodily from one to another. Both forms are very useful; but as far as complex computations are concerned, both are still in embryo.
blocks.zh: 加法只是一种运算。算术计算还包括减法、乘法和除法，此外还需要某种暂存结果、从存储中取出结果继续处理，以及打印最终结果的方法。这些用途的机器目前有两种：用于会计等工作的键盘机器，数据输入由人工控制，运算顺序通常自动控制；以及穿孔卡片机器，各种独立运算通常交给一系列机器，卡片随后在机器之间实际搬运。两种形式都很有用，但对于复杂计算而言，两者仍处于萌芽阶段。

blocks.en: Rapid electrical counting appeared soon after the physicists found it desirable to count cosmic rays. For their own purposes the physicists promptly constructed thermionic-tube equipment capable of counting electrical impulses at the rate of 100,000 a second. The advanced arithmetical machines of the future will be electrical in nature, and they will perform at 100 times present speeds, or more.
blocks.zh: 物理学家发现需要计数宇宙射线之后不久，快速电计数就出现了。为了自身目的，物理学家迅速制造出热电子管设备，每秒能计数十万个电脉冲。未来先进的算术机器将是电气性质的，运算速度将是当前的一百倍，甚至更快。

blocks.en: Moreover, they will be far more versatile than present commercial machines, so that they may readily be adapted for a wide variety of operations. They will be controlled by a control card or film, they will select their own data and manipulate it in accordance with the instructions thus inserted, they will perform complex arithmetical computations at exceedingly high speeds, and they will record results in such form as to be readily available for distribution or for later further manipulation. Such machines will have enormous appetites. One of them will take instructions and data from a whole roomful of girls armed with simple key board punches, and will deliver sheets of computed results every few minutes. There will always be plenty of things to compute in the detailed affairs of millions of people doing complicated things.
blocks.zh: 而且，它们会比现有商用机器灵活得多，能方便地适应多种运算。它们由控制卡片或胶片控制，自行选择数据，依据这样输入的指令进行处理，以极高速度完成复杂算术计算，并以便于分发或继续处理的形式记录结果。这些机器会有惊人的胃口：一台机器就能接收一整间屋子的姑娘用简单键盘打孔机准备的指令和数据，每隔几分钟便输出成页的计算结果。数百万人从事复杂事务，其细节之中，总会有大量事情需要计算。
四

blocks.en: The repetitive processes of thought are not confined however, to matters of arithmetic and statistics. In fact, every time one combines and records facts in accordance with established logical processes, the creative aspect of thinking is concerned only with the selection of the data and the process to be employed and the manipulation thereafter is repetitive in nature and hence a fit matter to be relegated to the machine. Not so much has been done along these lines,beyond the bounds of arithmetic, as might be done, primarily because of the economics of the situation. The needs of business and the extensive market obviously waiting, assured the advent of mass-produced arithmetical machines just as soon as production methods were sufficiently advanced.
blocks.zh: 不过，重复性思维过程并不限于算术和统计。事实上，每当人们依照既定逻辑过程组合并记录事实，思考的创造性方面只涉及数据和所用过程的选择，之后的处理本质上都是重复性的，因此适合交给机器。超出算术范围，在这些方面做的工作还远少于可能做到的，主要因为经济条件。商业需要和明显存在的广阔市场，使算术机器在生产方法足够先进后，立即得以大量制造。

blocks.en: With machines for advanced analysis no such situation existed; for there was and is no extensive market; the users of advanced methods of manipulating data are a very small part of the population. There are, however, machines for solving differential equations—and functional and integral equations, for that matter. There are many special machines, such as the harmonic synthesizer which predicts the tides. There will be many more, appearing certainly first in the hands of the scientist and in small numbers.
blocks.zh: 高等分析机器没有这样的条件，因为过去没有、现在也没有广阔市场；使用高等数据处理方法的人，在人口中只占极小部分。不过，已经有解微分方程的机器，也有解函数方程和积分方程的机器。还有许多专用机器，例如预测潮汐的谐波合成器。未来会出现更多，最初肯定数量不多，并由科学家使用。

blocks.en: If scientific reasoning were limited to the logical processes of arithmetic, we should not get far in our understanding of the physical world. One might as well attempt to grasp the game of poker entirely by the use of the mathematics of probability. The abacus, with its beads strung on parallel wires, led the Arabs to positional numeration and the concept of zero many centuries before the rest of the world; and it was a useful tool—so useful that it still exists.
blocks.zh: 如果科学推理仅限于算术的逻辑过程，我们对物理世界的理解就走不了多远。这就好比只靠概率数学来理解扑克游戏。珠子穿在平行金属丝上的算盘，使阿拉伯人比世界其他地区早几个世纪获得位值记数法和零的概念；它还是一种有用的工具——有用到今天仍然存在。

blocks.en: It is a far cry from the abacus to the modern keyboard accounting machine. It will be an equal step to the arithmetical machine of the future. But even this new machine will not take the scientist where he needs to go. Relief must be secured from laborious detailed manipulation of higher mathematics as well, if the users of it are to free their brains for something more than repetitive detailed transformations in accordance with established rules. A mathematician is not a man who can readily manipulate figures; often he cannot. He is not even a man who can readily perform the transformations of equations by the use of calculus. He is primarily an individual who is skilled in the use of symbolic logic on a high plane, and especially he is a man of intuitive judgment in the choice of the manipulative processes he employs.
blocks.zh: 从算盘到现代键盘式会计机器，跨越很大；从后者到未来算术机器，也会是同样大的一步。但即便这台新机器，也不能把科学家带到他需要到达的地方。还必须把高等数学中繁重的细节处理工作解脱出来，才能让使用者的大脑去做比依照既定规则反复变换细节更多的事情。数学家并不是能够轻松处理数字的人；他往往不能。他甚至不只是能够运用微积分熟练变换方程的人。他首先是在高层次上熟练运用符号逻辑的人，尤其是在选择所采用的处理过程时具有直觉判断力的人。

blocks.en: All else he should be able to turn over to his mechanism, just as confidently as he turns over the propelling of his car to the intricate mechanism under the hood. Only then will mathematics be practically effective in bringing the growing knowledge of atomistics to the useful solution of the advanced problems of chemistry, metallurgy, and biology. For this reason there still come more machines to handle advanced mathematics for the scientist. Some of them will be sufficiently bizarre to suit the most fastidious connoisseur of the present artifacts of civilization.
blocks.zh: 其余一切，他都应当能够交给机器，就像放心把汽车的驱动交给引擎盖下复杂的机械一样。只有这样，数学才能切实有效地把不断增长的原子科学知识，用于解决化学、冶金和生物学中的高等问题。因此，还会出现更多为科学家处理高等数学的机器。其中一些会足够奇异，满足对当今文明造物最挑剔的鉴赏者。
五

blocks.en: The scientist, however, is not the only person who manipulates data and examines the world about him by the use of logical processes, although he sometimes preserves this appearance by adopting into the fold anyone who becomes logical, much in the manner in which a British labor leader is elevated to knighthood. Whenever logical processes of thought are employed—that is, whenever thought for a time runs along an accepted groove—there is an opportunity for the machine. Formal logic used to be a keen instrument in the hands of the teacher in his trying of students' souls. It is readily possible to construct a machine which will manipulate premises in accordance with formal logic, simply by the clever use of relay circuits. Put a set of premises into such a device and turn the crank, and it will readily pass out conclusion after conclusion, all in accordance with logical law, and with no more slips than would be expected of a keyboard adding machine.
blocks.zh: 不过，科学家并非唯一用逻辑过程处理数据、审视周围世界的人，虽然他有时会把任何变得有逻辑的人都吸收为同类，以维持这种表象，有些像英国工党领袖被授予骑士称号。凡运用逻辑思维过程之处——也就是思考暂时沿着公认轨道运行之处——都有机器发挥作用的机会。形式逻辑曾是教师用来考验学生灵魂的锋利工具。只要巧妙运用继电器电路，就很容易造出一台依照形式逻辑处理前提的机器。把一组前提输入装置，转动曲柄，它就能轻易输出一个又一个结论，全部符合逻辑法则，出错不会比键盘式加法机更多。

blocks.en: Logic can become enormously difficult, and it would undoubtedly be well to produce more assurance in its use. The machines for higher analysis have usually been equation solvers. Ideas are beginning to appear for equation transformers, which will rearrange the relationship expressed by an equation in accordance with strict and rather advanced logic. Progress is inhibited by the exceedingly crude way in which mathematicians express their relationships. They employ a symbolism which grew like Topsy and has little consistency; a strange fact in that most logical field.
blocks.zh: 逻辑可以变得极其困难，无疑应当让它的运用更可靠。高等分析机器通常用于求解方程。现在开始出现方程变换机的构想，它们依照严格、相当高等的逻辑，重新排列方程表达的关系。进步受到阻碍，是因为数学家表达关系的方式极为粗糙。他们使用的符号像托普西一样自行生长，几乎没有一致性；这在最有逻辑的领域中，是一件奇怪的事。

blocks.en: A new symbolism, probably positional, must apparently precede the reduction of mathematical transformations to machine processes. Then, on beyond the strict logic of the mathematician, lies the application of logic in everyday affairs. We may some day click off arguments on a machine with the same assurance that we now enter sales on a cash register. But the machine of logic will not look like a cash register, even of the streamlined model.
blocks.zh: 显然，在把数学变换变成机器过程之前，必须先有一套新符号，大概是按位置表示的符号。再往前，超越数学家的严格逻辑，就是逻辑在日常事务中的运用。有一天，我们也许能像今天把销售额输入收银机一样，满怀信心地在机器上按出论证。但逻辑机器看起来不会像收银机，甚至不会像流线型收银机。

blocks.en: So much for the manipulation of ideas and their insertion into the record. Thus far we seem to be worse off than before—for we can enormously extend the record; yet even in its present bulk we can hardly consult it. This is a much larger matter than merely the extraction of data for the purposes of scientific research; it involves the entire process by which man profits by his inheritance of acquired knowledge. The prime action of use is selection, and here we are halting indeed. There may be millions of fine thoughts, and the account of the experience on which they are based, all encased within stone walls of acceptable architectural form; but if the scholar can get at only one a week by diligent search, his syntheses are not likely to keep up with the current scene.
blocks.zh: 关于思想的处理及其进入记录，就说到这里。到目前为止，我们似乎比从前更糟了：我们能够大幅扩展记录，然而连它当前的规模都已经难以查阅。这远不只是为了科学研究抽取数据的问题；它涉及人类从继承的知识中获益的整个过程。使用的首要行动是选择，而我们在这里实在举步维艰。也许有数百万个精妙思想，以及它们所依据的经验记录，都被收藏在建筑形式合宜的石墙之内；但如果学者费力搜寻，每周也只能找到一个，他的综合研究就不大可能跟上当前的局面。

blocks.en: Selection, in this broad sense, is a stone adze in the hands of a cabinetmaker. Yet, in a narrow sense and in other areas, something has already been done mechanically on selection. The personnel officer of a factory drops a stack of a few thousand employee cards into a selecting machine, sets a code in accordance with an established convention, and produces in a short time a list of all employees who live in Trenton and know Spanish. Even such devices are much too slow when it comes, for example, to matching a set of fingerprints with one of five million on file. Selection devices of this sort will soon be speeded up from their present rate of reviewing data at a few hundred a minute. By the use of photocells and microfilm they will survey items at the rate of a thousand a second, and will print out duplicates of those selected. This process, however, is simple selection: it proceeds by examining in turn every one of a large set of items, and by picking out those which have certain specified characteristics. There is another form of selection best illustrated by the automatic telephone exchange. You dial a number and the machine selects and connects just one of a million possible stations. It does not run over them all. It pays attention only to a class given by a first digit, then only to a subclass of this given by the second digit, and so on; and thus proceeds rapidly and almost unerringly to the selected station. It requires a few seconds to make the selection, although the process could be speeded up if increased speed were economically warranted. If necessary, it could be made extremely fast by substituting thermionic-tube switching for mechanical switching, so that the full selection could be made in one one-hundredth of a second. No one would wish to spend the money necessary to make this change in the telephone system, but the general idea is applicable elsewhere.
blocks.zh: 这种广义上的选择，就像把石锛交给家具匠。然而，在较狭义的选择和其他领域中，机械化已经有所作为。工厂人事主管把几千张员工卡片投入选择机，按既定约定设定代码，很快便得到一份住在特伦顿且懂西班牙语的全部员工名单。但若要把一组指纹与存档的五百万组指纹之一匹配，这种装置仍太慢。此类选择装置，很快会从目前每分钟查阅数百条数据的速度加快。利用光电池和缩微胶片，它们将每秒查看一千条，并打印所选条目的副本。不过，这只是简单选择：依次检查大量条目中的每一条，挑出具有指定特征的条目。另一种选择形式，自动电话交换机最能说明。你拨一个号码，机器便从一百万个可能的电话站中选择并连接一个。它不会逐个检查，而只关注第一个数字指定的一类，再关注第二个数字指定的子类，以此类推，迅速而几乎无误地到达所选站点。选择需要几秒；如果经济上值得提高速度，还可以加快。必要时，用热电子管开关替代机械开关，就能极大加速，在百分之一秒内完成全部选择。没有人愿意为电话系统的这种改变花费所需资金，但这个一般思路可以用于别处。

blocks.en: Take the prosaic problem of the great department store. Every time a charge sale is made, there are a number of things to be done. The inventory needs to be revised, the salesman needs to be given credit for the sale, the general accounts need an entry, and, most important, the customer needs to be charged. A central records device has been developed in which much of this work is done conveniently. The salesman places on a stand the customer's identification card, his own card, and the card taken from the article sold—all punched cards. When he pulls a lever, contacts are made through the holes, machinery at a central point makes the necessary computations and entries, and the proper receipt is printed for the salesman to pass to the customer.
blocks.zh: 以大型百货商店这个普通问题为例。每次发生赊账销售，都有几件事情要做：修改库存，把销售记在售货员名下，在总账中登记，最重要的是向顾客记账。已经开发出一种中央记录装置，能够方便地完成其中许多工作。售货员把顾客身份卡、自己的卡，以及从售出商品上取下的卡放在一个架子上——全都是穿孔卡片。他拉动杠杆，触点穿过卡孔接通，中央位置的机器完成必要计算与登记，打印出适当的收据，由售货员交给顾客。

blocks.en: But there may be ten thousand charge customers doing business with the store, and before the full operation can be completed someone has to select the right card and insert it at the central office. Now rapid selection can slide just the proper card into position in an instant or two, and return it afterward. Another difficulty occurs, however. Someone must read a total on the card, so that the machine can add its computed item to it. Conceivably the cards might be of the dry photography type I have described. Existing totals could then be read by photocell, and the new total entered by an electron beam.
blocks.zh: 然而，与商店交易的赊账顾客可能有一万人。在整个操作完成之前，还得有人选择正确卡片，并把它插入中央办公室的装置。如今，快速选择能够在一两瞬间把正确卡片滑到所需位置，之后再送回。但还有一个困难：必须有人读出卡片上的合计数，机器才能把计算出的项目加上去。可以设想，卡片采用我前面描述的干式摄影类型。这样，就能用光电池读取现有合计，用电子束写入新的合计。

blocks.en: The cards may be in miniature, so that they occupy little space. They must move quickly. They need not be transferred far, but merely into position so that the photocell and recorder can operate on them. Positional dots can enter the data. At the end of the month a machine can readily be made to read these and to print an ordinary bill. With tube selection, in which no mechanical parts are involved in the switches, little time need be occupied in bringing the correct card into use—a second should suffice for the entire operation. The whole record on the card may be made by magnetic dots on a steel sheet if desired, instead of dots to be observed optically, following the scheme by which Poulsen long ago put speech on a magnetic wire. This method has the advantage of simplicity and ease of erasure. By using photography, however one can arrange to project the record in enlarged form and at a distance by using the process common in television equipment.
blocks.zh: 卡片可以微型化，只占很小空间。它们必须迅速移动，不必搬得很远，只需移到光电池和记录器能够处理的位置。数据可以用按位置排列的点输入。到月底，很容易造出一台机器读取这些数据，并打印普通账单。用电子管进行选择，开关中没有机械部件，就不必花太多时间把正确卡片调来使用——整个操作一秒应当足够。如果愿意，卡片上的全部记录，也可以采用钢片上的磁性点，而非供光学观察的点，沿用波尔森很早把语音记录在磁性金属丝上的方案。这种方法具有简单、易于擦除的优点。不过，使用摄影，则可以利用电视设备中常见的过程，把记录放大并投射到远处。

blocks.en: One can consider rapid selection of this form, and distant projection for other purposes. To be able to key one sheet of a million before an operator in a second or two, with the possibility of then adding notes thereto, is suggestive in many ways. It might even be of use in libraries, but that is another story. At any rate, there are now some interesting combinations possible. One might, for example, speak to a microphone, in the manner described in connection with the speech controlled typewriter, and thus make his selections. It would certainly beat the usual file clerk.
blocks.zh: 可以把这种快速选择与远距离投影用于其他目的。在一两秒内，从百万页中调出一页呈现在操作者面前，而且随后还能添加笔记，这在许多方面都很有启发性。它甚至可能用于图书馆，不过那是另一个话题。无论如何，现在已经可以进行一些有趣的组合。例如，按照前面讨论语音控制打字机时所述的方式，对麦克风讲话，从而完成选择。这当然会胜过通常的档案管理员。
六

blocks.en: The real heart of the matter of selection, however, goes deeper than a lag in the adoption of mechanisms by libraries, or a lack of development of devices for their use. Our ineptitude in getting at the record is largely caused by the artificiality of systems of indexing. When data of any sort are placed in storage, they are filed alphabetically or numerically, and information is found (when it is) by tracing it down from subclass to subclass. It can be in only one place, unless duplicates are used; one has to have rules as to which path will locate it, and the rules are cumbersome. Having found one item, moreover, one has to emerge from the system and re-enter on a new path.
blocks.zh: 然而，选择问题真正的核心，比图书馆采用机械装置的迟缓，或适用设备发展不足，更为深刻。我们获取记录的能力很差，很大程度上源于索引系统的人为性。任何数据进入存储后，都按字母或数字归档；要找到信息——如果找得到——就必须沿着一个又一个子类向下追踪。除非制作副本，它只能放在一个地方；必须规定沿哪条路径才能找到，而这些规则十分繁琐。此外，找到一个条目后，还必须退出系统，再沿一条新路径重新进入。

blocks.en: The human mind does not work that way. It operates by association. With one item in its grasp, it snaps instantly to the next that is suggested by the association of thoughts, in accordance with some intricate web of trails carried by the cells of the brain. It has other characteristics, of course; trails that are not frequently followed are prone to fade, items are not fully permanent, memory is transitory. Yet the speed of action, the intricacy of trails, the detail of mental pictures, is awe-inspiring beyond all else in nature.
blocks.zh: 人类头脑不是这样工作的。它依靠联想运行。抓住一个条目后，便按照脑细胞中复杂的路径网络，沿着思想联想的提示，立刻跳到下一个条目。当然，它还有其他特点：不常走的路径容易消退，条目并不完全永久，记忆会流逝。不过，行动的速度、路径的复杂程度，以及心中图像的细节，比自然界其他一切都更令人敬畏。

blocks.en: Man cannot hope fully to duplicate this mental process artificially, but he certainly ought to be able to learn from it. In minor ways he may even improve, for his records have relative permanency. The first idea, however, to be drawn from the analogy concerns selection. Selection by association, rather than indexing, may yet be mechanized. One cannot hope thus to equal the speed and flexibility with which the mind follows an associative trail, but it should be possible to beat the mind decisively in regard to the permanence and clarity of the items resurrected from storage.
blocks.zh: 人类不能指望用人工方式完全复制这一心理过程，但肯定应当能够从中学习。在一些小方面，甚至可能改进它，因为人的外部记录具有相对持久性。不过，从这个类比中首先得到的思路，是关于选择的。依靠联想而非索引进行选择，也许也能机械化。我们不能期望这样达到头脑沿联想路径运行的速度和灵活性，但在从存储中重新唤起条目的持久性与清晰性方面，应当能够决定性地胜过头脑。

blocks.en: Consider a future device for individual use, which is a sort of mechanized private file and library. It needs a name, and, to coin one at random, "memex" will do. A memex is a device in which an individual stores all his books, records, and communications, and which is mechanized so that it may be consulted with exceeding speed and flexibility. It is an enlarged intimate supplement to his memory.
blocks.zh: 设想一种供个人使用的未来装置，类似机械化的私人档案与图书馆。它需要一个名字，随意造一个，“memex”就可以。Memex是一种装置，个人在其中储存自己的全部书籍、记录和通信；它经过机械化，能够以极高的速度和灵活性查阅。它是个人记忆的一种扩展而亲密的补充。

blocks.en: It consists of a desk, and while it can presumably be operated from a distance, it is primarily the piece of furniture at which he works. On the top are slanting translucent screens, on which material can be projected for convenient reading. There is a keyboard, and sets of buttons and levers. Otherwise it looks like an ordinary desk.
blocks.zh: 它由一张书桌组成；虽然大概可以远程操作，但它主要是使用者工作时所坐的那件家具。桌面上有倾斜的半透明屏幕，可以把资料投影其上，便于阅读。有一个键盘，以及几组按钮和杠杆。除此之外，它看起来与普通书桌无异。

blocks.en: In one end is the stored material. The matter of bulk is well taken care of by improved microfilm. Only a small part of the interior of the memex is devoted to storage, the rest to mechanism. Yet if the user inserted 5000 pages of material a day it would take him hundreds of years to fill the repository, so he can be profligate and enter material freely.
blocks.zh: 储存的资料位于一端。改进的缩微胶片很好地解决了体积问题。Memex内部只有很小一部分用于存储，其余用于机械机构。不过，即使使用者每天输入五千页资料，也要几百年才能填满这个储存库，因此他可以毫不吝惜地自由输入资料。

blocks.en: Most of the memex contents are purchased on microfilm ready for insertion. Books of all sorts, pictures, current periodicals, newspapers, are thus obtained and dropped into place. Business correspondence takes the same path. And there is provision for direct entry. On the top of the memex is a transparent platen. On this are placed longhand notes, photographs, memoranda, all sorts of things. When one is in place, the depression of a lever causes it to be photographed onto the next blank space in a section of the memex film, dry photography being employed.
blocks.zh: Memex的大多数内容，购买时就已制成可直接装入的缩微胶片。各类书籍、图片、当期期刊、报纸，都以这种方式获得并放入装置。业务通信也走同一条路径。此外，还提供直接输入的方法。Memex顶部有一个透明压板，可以放手写笔记、照片、备忘录，以及各种东西。把一项资料放好，压下杠杆，就会用干式摄影，把它拍到Memex某段胶片的下一个空白位置。

blocks.en: There is, of course, provision for consultation of the record by the usual scheme of indexing. If the user wishes to consult a certain book, he taps its code on the keyboard, and the title page of the book promptly appears before him, projected onto one of his viewing positions. Frequently-used codes are mnemonic, so that he seldom consults his code book; but when he does, a single tap of a key projects it for his use. Moreover, he has supplemental levers. On deflecting one of these levers to the right he runs through the book before him, each page in turn being projected at a speed which just allows a recognizing glance at each. If he deflects it further to the right, he steps through the book 10 pages at a time; still further at 100 pages at a time. Deflection to the left gives him the same control backwards.
blocks.zh: 当然，也能用通常的索引方式查阅记录。如果用户想看某本书，便在键盘上输入它的代码，书的扉页就立即投射到一个查看位置，出现在眼前。常用代码具有助记性，因此很少需要查代码簿；即使需要，只按一个键就能把代码簿投影出来。此外，还有辅助杠杆。把其中一根向右拨，便能浏览眼前的书，各页依次投射，速度刚好容许每页扫上一眼。继续向右拨，就一次翻十页；再远一些，就一次翻一百页。向左拨，则以同样方式向后控制。

blocks.en: A special button transfers him immediately to the first page of the index. Any given book of his library can thus be called up and consulted with far greater facility than if it were taken from a shelf. As he has several projection positions, he can leave one item in position while he calls up another. He can add marginal notes and comments, taking advantage of one possible type of dry photography, and it could even be arranged so that he can do this by a stylus scheme, such as is now employed in the telautograph seen in railroad waiting rooms, just as though he had the physical page before him.
blocks.zh: 一个专用按钮，可以立即跳到索引首页。这样，藏书中任何一本都能被调出、查阅，比从书架取下方便得多。由于有多个投影位置，可以让一个条目留在原处，同时调出另一个。利用某种可能的干式摄影方式，还能添加边注与评论；甚至可以设计成使用触笔，就像如今火车候车室里见到的传写电报机，让人仿佛面对真实的纸页。
七

blocks.en: All this is conventional, except for the projection forward of present-day mechanisms and gadgetry. It affords an immediate step, however, to associative indexing, the basic idea of which is a provision whereby any item may be caused at will to select immediately and automatically another. This is the essential feature of the memex. The process of tying two items together is the important thing.
blocks.zh: 除了把当前机械装置与小器具向未来推演，这一切都是传统做法。不过，它立即引出了联想索引：其基本思想是，提供一种机制，让任何条目都能按意愿立即、自动地选择另一个条目。这是Memex的核心特征。重要的是把两个条目连接起来的过程。

blocks.en: When the user is building a trail, he names it, inserts the name in his code book, and taps it out on his keyboard. Before him are the two items to be joined, projected onto adjacent viewing positions. At the bottom of each there are a number of blank code spaces, and a pointer is set to indicate one of these on each item. The user taps a single key, and the items are permanently joined. In each code space appears the code word. Out of view, but also in the code space, is inserted a set of dots for photocell viewing; and on each item these dots by their positions designate the index number of the other item.
blocks.zh: 用户建立一条路径时，先给它命名，把名字写进代码簿，再在键盘上输入。要连接的两个条目投影在相邻的查看位置，出现在面前。每个条目的底部都有一些空白代码位置，指针分别指向其中一个。用户只按一次键，两个条目就永久连接。在每个代码位置上都出现那个代码词。在看不见的地方，但也在代码位置中，会插入一组供光电池读取的点；在每个条目上，这些点的位置标明另一个条目的索引编号。

blocks.en: Thereafter, at any time, when one of these items is in view, the other can be instantly recalled merely by tapping a button below the corresponding code space. Moreover, when numerous items have been thus joined together to form a trail, they can be reviewed in turn, rapidly or slowly, by deflecting a lever like that used for turning the pages of a book. It is exactly as though the physical items had been gathered together from widely separated sources and bound together to form a new book. It is more than this, for any item can be joined into numerous trails.
blocks.zh: 此后，任何时候，只要一个条目正在显示，按一下相应代码位置下方的按钮，就能立即调出另一个。而且，当许多条目以这种方式连接成一条路径时，就能像翻书那样拨动杠杆，快速或缓慢地依次查看。效果正如把来自相距甚远来源的实际资料汇集起来，装订成一本新书。它还不止如此，因为任何条目都能加入多条路径。

blocks.en: The owner of the memex, let us say, is interested in the origin and properties of the bow and arrow. Specifically he is studying why the short Turkish bow was apparently superior to the English long bow in the skirmishes of the Crusades. He has dozens of possibly pertinent books and articles in his memex. First he runs through an encyclopedia, finds an interesting but sketchy article, leaves it projected. Next, in a history, he finds another pertinent item, and ties the two together. Thus he goes, building a trail of many items. Occasionally he inserts a comment of his own, either linking it into the main trail or joining it by a side trail to a particular item. When it becomes evident that the elastic properties of available materials had a great deal to do with the bow, he branches off on a side trail which takes him through textbooks on elasticity and tables of physical constants. He inserts a page of longhand analysis of his own. Thus he builds a trail of his interest through the maze of materials available to him.
blocks.zh: 比如说，Memex的主人对弓箭的起源与性质感兴趣。他具体研究的是，为什么在十字军东征的小规模战斗中，土耳其短弓似乎优于英国长弓。他的Memex中有几十本可能相关的书和文章。他先浏览百科全书，找到一篇有趣但粗略的文章，让它保持投影。接着，在一本历史书中找到另一项相关资料，并把两者连接。他如此继续，建立起包含许多条目的路径。偶尔加入自己的评论，或者连入主路径，或者用支线连接到某个特定条目。当他发现可用材料的弹性与弓大有关系时，就分出一条支线，沿弹性教科书和物理常数表浏览。他加入一页自己的手写分析。这样，他就在可用资料的迷宫中，建立一条符合自身兴趣的路径。

blocks.en: And his trails do not fade. Several years later, his talk with a friend turns to the queer ways in which a people resist innovations, even of vital interest. He has an example, in the fact that the outraged Europeans still failed to adopt the Turkish bow. In fact he has a trail on it. A touch brings up the code book. Tapping a few keys projects the head of the trail. A lever runs through it at will, stopping at interesting items, going off on side excursions. It is an interesting trail, pertinent to the discussion. So he sets a reproducer in action, photographs the whole trail out, and passes it to his friend for insertion in his own memex, there to be linked into the more general trail.
blocks.zh: 而他的路径不会消退。几年之后，他与朋友谈到一个民族抵制创新的奇怪方式，即便创新关乎重大利益。他有一个例子：愤怒的欧洲人仍然没有采用土耳其弓。事实上，他还有关于此事的一条路径。轻按一下，代码簿就出现了。再按几个键，路径的开头便投影出来。一根杠杆让他随意浏览，在有趣条目处停下，也能转入支线。这条路径很有趣，与讨论相关。于是，他启动复制器，把整条路径拍出来，交给朋友装进自己的Memex，并在那里接入更一般的路径。
八

blocks.en: Wholly new forms of encyclopedias will appear, ready made with a mesh of associative trails running through them, ready to be dropped into the memex and there amplified. The lawyer has at his touch the associated opinions and decisions of his whole experience, and of the experience of friends and authorities. The patent attorney has on call the millions of issued patents, with familiar trails to every point of his client's interest. The physician, puzzled by a patient's reactions, strikes the trail established in studying an earlier similar case, and runs rapidly through analogous case histories, with side references to the classics for the pertinent anatomy and histology. The chemist, struggling with the synthesis of an organic compound, has all the chemical literature before him in his laboratory, with trails following the analogies of compounds, and side trails to their physical and chemical behavior.
blocks.zh: 将出现全新形式的百科全书：预先贯穿联想路径网络，随时可以装入Memex，再在那里扩展。律师触手可及地掌握自身全部经验，以及朋友和权威经验中相互关联的意见与判决。专利律师能够随时调阅数百万项已授予专利，并沿熟悉的路径到达客户感兴趣的每个方面。医生对病人的反应感到困惑时，可以进入研究此前类似病例时建立的路径，迅速浏览相似病史，并沿支线查阅经典著作中相关的解剖学与组织学内容。化学家为合成一种有机化合物苦苦思索时，全部化学文献就在实验室面前，路径连接着类似化合物，支线通向它们的物理和化学行为。

blocks.en: The historian, with a vast chronological account of a people, parallels it with a skip trail which stops only on the salient items, and can follow at any time contemporary trails which lead him all over civilization at a particular epoch. There is a new profession of trail blazers, those who find delight in the task of establishing useful trails through the enormous mass of the common record. The inheritance from the master becomes, not only his additions to the world's record, but for his disciples the entire scaffolding by which they were erected.
blocks.zh: 历史学家面对一份关于某个民族的庞大编年记录，可以同时使用一条只停留于要点的跳跃路径，并随时沿当时的路径，走遍某一时代的文明。还会出现一种新职业——路径开拓者；这些人乐于在庞大的公共记录中建立有用的路径。大师传给弟子的遗产，不仅是他为世界记录增添的内容，还包括建立这些内容所凭借的整个支架。

blocks.en: Thus science may implement the ways in which man produces, stores, and consults the record of the race. It might be striking to outline the instrumentalities of the future more spectacularly, rather than to stick closely to methods and elements now known and undergoing rapid development, as has been done here. Technical difficulties of all sorts have been ignored, certainly, but also ignored are means as yet unknown which may come any day to accelerate technical progress as violently as did the advent of the thermionic tube. In order that the picture may not be too commonplace, by reason of sticking to present-day patterns, it may be well to mention one such possibility, not to prophesy but merely to suggest, for prophecy based on extension of the known has substance, while prophecy founded on the unknown is only a doubly involved guess.
blocks.zh: 这样，科学可以改进人类制作、储存和查阅种族记录的方式。若把未来工具描绘得更壮观，而非像这里一样，紧贴目前已知且正在迅速发展的方法与组成部分，可能更引人注目。我们当然忽略了各种技术困难，但也忽略了那些尚不为人所知、随时可能出现的手段；它们可能像热电子管的出现一样，猛烈加速技术进步。为了避免因为紧贴当代模式而使图景过于平常，也许可以提到一种这样的可能性。这不是预言，只是提示；因为基于已知事物延伸的预言有所根据，而建立在未知之上的预言，不过是双重复杂的猜测。

blocks.en: All our steps in creating or absorbing material of the record proceed through one of the senses—the tactile when we touch keys, the oral when we speak or listen, the visual when we read. Is it not possible that some day the path may be established more directly?
blocks.zh: 我们制作或吸收记录资料的所有步骤，都经过某一种感官：触碰按键时经过触觉，说话或倾听时经过口耳，阅读时经过视觉。难道有一天，不能建立一条更直接的路径吗？

blocks.en: We know that when the eye sees, all the consequent information is transmitted to the brain by means of electrical vibrations in the channel of the optic nerve. This is an exact analogy with the electrical vibrations which occur in the cable of a television set: they convey the picture from the photocells which see it to the radio transmitter from which it is broadcast. We know further that if we can approach that cable with the proper instruments, we do not need to touch it; we can pick up those vibrations by electrical induction and thus discover and reproduce the scene which is being transmitted, just as a telephone wire may be tapped for its message.
blocks.zh: 我们知道，眼睛看见东西时，产生的全部信息都通过视神经通道中的电振动传入大脑。这与电视设备电缆中的电振动完全类似：电缆把图像从看见它的光电池，传送到用来广播的无线电发射器。我们还知道，只要用合适的仪器接近这条电缆，就无须触碰它；通过电感应即可拾取那些振动，从而发现并再现正在传输的场景，正如可以窃听电话线路上的信息。

blocks.en: The impulses which flow in the arm nerves of a typist convey to her fingers the translated information which reaches her eye or ear, in order that the fingers may be caused to strike the proper keys. Might not these currents be intercepted, either in the original form in which information is conveyed to the brain, or in the marvelously metamorphosed form in which they then proceed to the hand?
blocks.zh: 打字员手臂神经中流动的脉冲，把到达眼睛或耳朵的信息，转换后传给手指，使手指敲击正确的按键。难道这些电流不能被截取吗？可以截取信息传入大脑时的原始形式，也可以截取它们随后传向手部时，经过奇妙转换后的形式。

blocks.en: By bone conduction we already introduce sounds: into the nerve channels of the deaf in order that they may hear. Is it not possible that we may learn to introduce them without the present cumbersomeness of first transforming electrical vibrations to mechanical ones, which the human mechanism promptly transforms back to the electrical form? With a couple of electrodes on the skull the encephalograph now produces pen-and-ink traces which bear some relation to the electrical phenomena going on in the brain itself. True, the record is unintelligible, except as it points out certain gross misfunctioning of the cerebral mechanism; but who would now place bounds on where such a thing may lead?
blocks.zh: 我们已经通过骨传导，把声音引入聋人的神经通道，让他们听见。难道我们不能学会直接引入它们，而无须像现在这样笨拙地先把电振动变成机械振动，再让人体机制立即把它转回电形式吗？如今，只需在颅骨上放几个电极，脑电图仪就能用笔墨画出轨迹，与大脑内部发生的电现象具有某种关系。诚然，除了指示某些明显的脑机制故障，这些记录还无法理解；但现在有谁能为这种事物未来的去向划定界限？

blocks.en: In the outside world, all forms of intelligence whether of sound or sight, have been reduced to the form of varying currents in an electric circuit in order that they may be transmitted. Inside the human frame exactly the same sort of process occurs. Must we always transform to mechanical movements in order to proceed from one electrical phenomenon to another? It is a suggestive thought, but it hardly warrants prediction without losing touch with reality and immediateness.
blocks.zh: 在外部世界，各种形式的信息，无论声音还是图像，都被转化为电路中变化的电流，以便传输。在人体内部，也发生着完全同类的过程。我们从一种电现象转向另一种电现象时，是否总要转换为机械运动？这是一个很有启发性的想法，但如果不想脱离现实与眼前情况，还不足以据此作出预言。

blocks.en: Presumably man's spirit should be elevated if he can better review his shady past and analyze more completely and objectively his present problems. He has built a civilization so complex that he needs to mechanize his records more fully if he is to push his experiment to its logical conclusion and not merely become bogged down part way there by overtaxing his limited memory. His excursions may be more enjoyable if he can reacquire the privilege of forgetting the manifold things he does not need to have immediately at hand, with some assurance that he can find them again if they prove important.
blocks.zh: 如果人能更好地回顾自己阴暗的过去，更完整、客观地分析当前问题，他的精神大概应当得到提升。他建立了如此复杂的文明，如果要把这项实验推向其逻辑终点，而不在半途中因有限记忆负担过重而陷入泥潭，就需要更充分地机械化自己的记录。如果他能重新获得遗忘许多不必立即放在手边事物的权利，并确信它们若证明重要还可以找回，那么他的探索也许会更加愉快。

blocks.en: The applications of science have built man a well-supplied house, and are teaching him to live healthily therein. They have enabled him to throw masses of people against one another with cruel weapons. They may yet allow him truly to encompass the great record and to grow in the wisdom of race experience. He may perish in conflict before he learns to wield that record for his true good. Yet, in the application of science to the needs and desires of man, it would seem to be a singularly unfortunate stage at which to terminate the process, or to lose hope as to the outcome.
blocks.zh: 科学的应用为人类建造了一座供给充足的房屋，并教他在其中健康地生活。它们也使人能够用残酷武器，把大批人推向彼此对抗。它们或许最终还能让人真正掌握宏大的记录，并从人类经验中增长智慧。在学会为自身真正的利益运用记录之前，人可能就在冲突中灭亡。然而，在把科学应用于人类的需要与愿望这一过程里，若在此时终止进程，或对其结果失去希望，似乎是一个格外不幸的阶段。
